intro: Ireland punches far above its size in literature and music, and its festivals, from St Patrick's Day to Halloween, are celebrated worldwide.

chapters.title: Writers
text: Ireland has four Nobel Prize winners in Literature: W. B. Yeats, George Bernard Shaw, Samuel Beckett and Seamus Heaney. James Joyce, Oscar Wilde, Jonathan Swift and Bram Stoker, author of Dracula, were also Irish.

chapters.title: Music and festivals
text: Traditional music uses the fiddle, tin whistle, bodhrán drum and uilleann pipes. U2, The Cranberries and Hozier are famous Irish acts, and Ireland has won Eurovision seven times, a joint record.
Halloween grew from the ancient Celtic festival of Samhain, which marked the start of winter.

keyTerms.meaning: A Celtic festival marking the end of harvest, the origin of Halloween.
